content:
Doris "Dorie" Miller (October 12, 1919 – November 24, 1943) was an American sailor in the U.S. Navy who became a hero during the attack on Pearl Harbor. Here's what's known about him:

## Early Life
- Born in Waco, Texas, to sharecropper parents Connery and Henrietta Miller
- One of four sons; named "Doris" by the midwife who expected a girl
- Worked on his family's farm and attended Moore High School, where he played fullback on the football team
- Enlisted in the U.S. Navy in September 1939 at age 19

## Naval Service
Due to the segregated Navy of that era, Black sailors were restricted to the Messman Branch, serving as cooks, stewards, and attendants. Miller was assigned as a Mess Attendant, Third Class, and eventually served aboard the USS West Virginia. He was the ship's heavyweight boxing champion.

## Pearl Harbor (December 7, 1941)
When the Japanese attacked, Miller was collecting laundry aboard the West Virginia. During the attack, he:
- Helped carry wounded sailors to safety, including the mortally wounded ship's captain, Mervyn Bennion
- Operated an unfamiliar .50 caliber anti-aircraft machine gun, despite having no training on the weapon (Black sailors were not trained in weaponry at the time)
- Fired at attacking Japanese aircraft until ordered to abandon ship
- He helped move other injured sailors through oil and water to greater safety

## Recognition
- Received the Navy Cross on May 27, 1942, from Admiral Chester W. Nimitz aboard the USS Enterprise — becoming the first African American to receive this honor
- Also received the Purple Heart, the American Defense Service Medal, Asiatic-Pacific Campaign Medal, and World War II Victory Medal
- Promoted to Mess Attendant First Class, and later to Ship's Cook Third Class

## Death
Miller was assigned to the escort carrier USS Liscome Bay. On November 24, 1943, the ship was torpedoed by Japanese submarine I-175 near Butaritari (Makin) Island. The ship sank rapidly with the loss of 646 crew members, including Miller. He was declared missing and presumed dead on November 25, 1944.

## Legacy
- USS Miller (FF-1091), a Knox-class frigate, was named after him in 1973
- In January 2020, the Navy announced that a new Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, CVN-81, would be named USS Doris Miller — the first aircraft carrier named after an African American and the first named after an enlisted sailor
- Featured in the films "Pearl Harbor" (2001), where he was portrayed by Cuba Gooding Jr., and "Tora! Tora! Tora!" (1970)
- Numerous schools, parks, and memorials have been named in his honor
- A campaign has long sought to upgrade his Navy Cross to the Medal of Honor

Miller is remembered as a symbol of heroism and as an important figure in the eventual desegregation of the U.S. military.
